Development of the MPAA's least-favorite app of the 2010s has been abandoned for years , but the "Netflix of Piracy" software is still installed on millions of devices that are just waiting to join a bot army. Researchers at Eye Security found the updater for a Popcorn Time fork called "Time4Popcorn" still running on tons of Windows, macOS, and Android devices located around the world, phoning home to now-abandoned web domains over unencrypted HTTP and running an outdated, insecure version of Chrome. Eye Security's Niels Teus … Read the full story at The Verge.

items.title: Elon Musk’s dangerous grip on outer space
items.snippet: Last week, Starshield - the version of SpaceX's Starlink used by the Ukrainian military - was throttled to block terminals traveling above certain speeds from accessing the service. The Ukrainian army's interceptors, which counter Russian drones carrying bombs, suddenly stopped working at high speeds, making it easier for Russia to attack the country's energy infrastructure and leading to a reported two deaths and at least 17 injuries . The Ukrainian military reported receiving no advance warning about the Starshield speed restriction. items.snippet: Well, that didn’t take long. As Apple’s iPhone Duo starts to land in the hands of early customers, copycat apps for the Duo’s most well-known features and apps are already landing on Android foldables – not that that’s a bad thing. One iPhone Duo feature that isn’t widely used on Android is the ability to show information while in “Tent Mode.” The Motorola Razr Fold is one of the few book-style foldables with this feature as a part of its always-on display, but the iPhone Duo’s “StandBy” mode is one that folks could easily want on other devices. Pixel also has similar functionality, but only while charging. A new Android app that delivers something pretty close to iPhone Duo’s tent mode is “Foldy.” The app is free to use, but requires a premium unlock (90¢/month or $9 lifetime) for its most useful features. On my Galaxy Z Fold 8, the app quickly let me turn tent mode into a useful dual-pane hub that shows the date and time, or data from my calendar. Night Shyamalan’s psychological thriller Servant. Starring Lauren Ambrose (Six Feet Under), Toby Kebbell (RocknRolla), Nell Tiger Free (The First Omen), and Rupert Grint (Snatch), the series “follows a Philadelphia couple in mourning after an unspeakable tragedy creates a rift in their marriage and opens the door for a mysterious force to enter their home,” per Apple TV’s synopsis. items.title: New PHP vulnerability means the Internet will have a very rough couple of days
items.snippet: A severe vulnerability has been found in key web technology PHP, forcing just about everybody to patch websites, and fast. Expect outages. Websites may go down for a few days because of a nasty PHP vulnerability. Over the next couple of days, there will be more complaints about websites being down than usual. It's not just you, but the effects of the Internet relying on PHP and something going horrifically wrong. The developers behind PHP, a web programming language, have said they will release a patch on Wednesday to fix a pair of vulnerabilities. They are rated at a very high 9.2 severity on the CVSSv4.0 severity scale. Continue Reading on AppleInsider | Discuss on our Forums

items.snippet: Macworld Apple unveiled the first iPod on October 23, 2001, exactly a quarter-century ago. items.snippet: Micron's G11 3D NAND promises 42 Gb/mm2 and 5,400 MT/s interface speed, enabling SSDs with extreme capacity and performance.

items.title: Illegal Nvidia Blackwell Ultra B300 GPUs found inside state-owned China Telecom's network
items.snippet: A security firm has been able to identify 32 Nvidia Blackwell Ultra B300 AI chips running inside a China Telecom network, but it's unclear where the export-barred components are physically located.

items.title: US banks scramble to restrict AI agent activity
items.snippet: Several U.S. banks are blocking AI agents from making transactions on their platforms. They fear that those agents could go rogue and there's no way to tell if the moves they make are legitimate or not.

items.title: Consultant comes clean for sparking worldwide panic by accidentally breaking the PHP vulnerability embargo
items.snippet: The user said that they only wanted to alert others about the importance of the upcoming CVE releases and weren't told about the embargo.

items.title: China-aligned hackers deploy AI agents in massive ConnectWise supply chain attack
items.snippet: Microsoft says China-aligned Storm-0940 used the ARTEX AI agent framework in the ConnectWise Cloud Backup supply chain attack.

items.title: Save $450 on this 4K gaming PC with an RTX 5070 Ti and 9800X3D, now $2,549.99

items.title: GPUs from stolen $470,000 Nvidia RTX 5090 shipment at Brazil airport appear for sale online, identified by serial numbers
items.snippet: One of the GPUs from a stolen shipment of RTX 5090 graphics cards has appeared for sale online. Police have identified three employees at an airport who stole the goods.

items.title: One easy change makes Microsoft's Surface Laptop Ultra with RTX Spark a better gaming system
items.snippet: Microsoft's Surface Laptop Ultra with RTX Spark might not be a gaming laptop first and foremost, but it certainly wants to game. We found that creating a custom 1920x1080-equivalent resolution for its 3:2 screen, missing from its out-of-the-box config, makes for a better experience.

items.title: AMD Ryzen 5 5500F review: Vermeer rides again for budget gaming PCs
items.snippet: After years with the Cezanne-based 5500, AMD has finally updated its $100 CPU to the 5500F in the Vermeer family, adding a 200 MHz boost in clock speed and a PCIe 4.0 upgrade.

items.title: Micron pulls the plug on future 4F² DRAM after two decades of research in dramatic shift
items.snippet: Micron believes that more advanced process technologies will present more benefits in terms of DRAM bit density than smaller memory cells.

items.title: Retro Atari VCS platform will end with the closure of its software store in February 2027
items.snippet: The modern Atari VCS is being officially retired with the firm’s decision to shut down the Linux-based AMD APU-powered machine's software store early next year.

items.title: Best Buy has slashed $950 off this gorgeous Alienware 16X Aurora gaming laptop with OLED display
items.snippet: Save 33% on a new Alienware 16X Aurora gaming laptop at Best Buy. RTX 5070 graphics and a sharp OLED panel are highlights of this laptop build.

items.title: Save $238 on this 9800X3D combo deal with 32GB DDR5 that lets you start a 4K gaming PC build for just over $1,000
items.snippet: This Newegg combo deal combines the AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D, 32GB of fast DDR5 RAM, and a Gigabyte AM5 X870E motherboard for $1,029.99, saving you over $238 in total.

items.title: 480,000 phishing emails sent from a PC hidden behind a fridge in a Japanese hotel room

items.title: Intel installs production tools at Fab 62 in Arizona, provides updates on Ohio chip fab

items.title: 4TB Samsung 990 Pro M.2 SSD falls 27%, hits 20 cents per gigabyte

items.title: AMD brings official Ryzen overclocking to Linux with AOD driver support
items.snippet: New driver enablement work from AMD brings full platform-level tuning control to Ryzen systems running Linux, finally.

items.title: Qualcomm to cut jobs globally in "performance-based" layoffs, as company pivots to AI data center and edge computing markets
items.snippet: Qualcomm will begin performance-based layoffs worldwide in November as the chipmaker reallocates resources toward AI infrastructure, data centers, automotive, PCs, and edge computing, amid weaker consumer electronics demand.

items.title: FADU puts the filesystem inside the SSD's flash to bypass host CPUs
items.snippet: FADU’s FS-SSD carries NFSv3 file operations inside NVMe commands, letting GPUs, DPUs, and NICs read files without a host file system.

items.title: AMD and Intel will work together to create a single PyTorch code path for AI inference on CPUs
items.snippet: AMD and Intel are working together to bring CPU inference optimizations for PyTorch under the unified oneDNN library.

items.title: Samsung and SK Hynix are upgrading Chinese factories to produce advanced RAM chips as AI data center competition ramps up
items.snippet: Samsung and SK Hynix are reportedly upgrading their factories to produce more advanced RAM chips designed for AI data centers in an attempt to fend off competition from Chinese companies.

items.title: Why you don't need an audiophile headset for gaming — comfort, convenience, and a good mic win over pure audio fidelity
items.snippet: Headsets are mainly about audio, but that doesn't mean that the "objectively" best-sounding headset by audiophile standards translates to the best-sounding headset by gaming standards.

items.title: Micron's Taiwan union will launch a one-day strike this week, threatening memory production
items.snippet: Micron's Taiwan union is set to conduct a one-day strike at the company's Taoyuan DRAM facility as workers demand bonuses for this year and transparent terms of bonuses for upcoming years.

items.title: Remediation in the era of AI: Fix what matters first
items.snippet: Every IT and security team knows the feeling of opening a vulnerability report and seeing a number that only goes up. Thousands of findings. Hundreds marked critical. A backlog that grows faster than any team can close it. For years, the default response has been to work harder: more scans, more tickets, more overtime. But the volume of vulnerabilities , accelerated by AI-assisted discovery and a sprawling mix of endpoints, cloud services, and applications, has outpaced that approach. items.title: The Patch Apocalypse is here. Patching everything isn’t the answer.
items.snippet: For most IT teams, Patch Tuesday used to set the rhythm of the month. Updates arrived, teams tested them, change boards approved them, and deployments rolled out over the following weeks. It wasn’t painless, but it was predictable. That predictability is gone. Nearly 48,000 CVEs were published in 2025 , and the average time to exploit has collapsed to roughly five days. Attackers no longer wait for organizations to finish their testing cycles. Move from reactive patching to risk-based automation → Many practitioners now call this the Patch Apocalypse. The name is dramatic, but the operational reality behind it is not. items.title: Rogue AI: When agents stop advising and start acting

That’s changing. Agentic AI systems can plan multistep tasks and carry them out: querying systems, triggering workflows, changing configurations, and closing tickets with little or no human involvement. Ivanti’s 2026 State of Cybersecurity Report found that 87% of security professionals say integrating agentic AI is a priority, and 77% report at least some comfort letting autonomous systems act without human review. items.title: AI isn’t hallucinating—but your data might be
items.snippet: “Hallucination” has become the catch-all term for AI getting things wrong. It describes a real phenomenon: Large language models can generate confident, fluent answers that are simply untrue. But in IT operations, many errors labeled as hallucinations have a more ordinary explanation. The AI isn’t inventing facts. It’s faithfully reporting information that happens to be outdated, incomplete, or contradictory. I’ve seen this play out across enough environments to know the cause usually sits upstream, in the data the system learned from and the picture of the estate it read. items.snippet: PHP has published a temporary mitigation for CVE-2026-115560, a remote code execution flaw that remains unpatched. items.title: x402 SDK flaws could expose AI agents’ full token balances
items.snippet: x402 lets software, including AI agents, pay for API calls directly through web requests. Before fixes released on August 18, its default clients had no spending cap, potentially letting a malicious API request an agent’s entire balance if payments were signed automatically and the app had no payment limits. The fixes also address two other critical flaws, but as of October 23, package audit tools did not flag the vulnerable releases. Source

items.title: Claude generates 180 million lines of proofs to check open-source code
items.snippet: Anthropic and verification firm Theorem used Claude to produce about 180 million lines of mathematical proofs for 239 program entry points across 123 open-source libraries. The proofs establish that 239 program entry points across 123 libraries won’t crash under the tested conditions. They don’t prove the libraries are universally correct or free of security flaws.The Rocq proof checker verified the results, while the work uncovered hundreds of bugs conventional testing had missed. The guarantees apply only under specific conditions, including inputs smaller than 64 MB. Source

items.title: Microsoft 365 token spraying hijacked 79 organizations without passwords
items.snippet: A ten-week token-spraying campaign broke into Microsoft 365 accounts at 79 organizations without stealing passwords, replaying sign-in sessions instead. Huntress counted 497 successful sign-ins among more than 200,000 attempts. Attackers then registered rogue devices, replaced victims’ MFA methods and hid emails with inbox rules. Source

PHP has fixed the flaws in versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35. Source

Alan Weckel, founder and analyst at 650 Group , is forecasting that data center switching revenue based on SONiC (Software for Open Networking in the Cloud) will exceed $5 billion in 2026 and that enterprise SONiC adoption will grow more than 25% year-over-year through 2027. Dell’Oro Group predicts that SONiC-based switch sales in AI scale-out networks will grow at more than 50 % a year through 2030, when revenues will exceed $10 billion. items.title: Microsoft expands sovereign cloud offerings as data control concerns grow
items.snippet: Microsoft expanded its sovereign cloud offerings on Tuesday, adding new security, governance and AI capabilities as customers, particularly in Europe, demand greater assurance over where data is stored, who can access it and how critical services operate during disruptions. The announcement builds on Microsoft’s ongoing digital sovereignty efforts, assisting organizations in applying appropriate levels of control to each workload rather than forcing a rigid, one-size-fits-all approach. “Organizations are considering more than where data resides. items.title: SONiC momentum continues at OCP Global Summit
items.snippet: Proponents of SONiC made a strong showing at last week’s Open Compute Project (OCP) Global Summit, where vendors including Cisco, Microsoft, and Nokia championed SONiC’s capabilities as an open Ethernet platform for AI networking. The Linux-based network operating system decouples network software from the underlying hardware and allows it to run on hundreds of switches and ASICs from multiple vendors. SONiC (which stands for Software for Open Networking in the Cloud) supports a full suite of network features, including Border Gateway Protocol (BGP), remote direct memory access (RDMA), QoS, and Ethernet/IP. items.title: Gartner’s top tech trends for 2027 expand—and constrain—AI capabilities
items.snippet: Gartner kicked off its IT Symposium/Xpo this week and unveiled its annual list of the top strategic technology trends that organizations need to explore in the coming year.
